headline: Welcome back—missing days doesn't break your learning, only stopping does
universal_truth: Every return is a fresh start; gaps in practice don't erase what you've built
fun_facts: Missing one day has almost no impact on long-term learning
The most successful learners aren't perfect—they're persistent after gaps
Guilt about missing keeps people away longer than the miss itself
discussion_questions: How are you feeling about being back?
What would help you maintain consistency going forward?

hook.script: You're back. That's what matters. However long you've been away, today you returned. That takes more courage than never missing at all. Welcome home.

cliff.script: It's tempting to feel guilty about the gap, or to think you've ruined your progress. What's the truth about missing days?

options.text: Gaps don't erase growth—what you learned is still there; the only way to truly fail is to stop entirely; returning after a gap is a sign of strength, not weakness
options.response: Exactly. Your brain doesn't delete learning when you miss days. The neural pathways remain. You're picking up a warm thread, not starting cold.
Not at all. Your foundation is still there. You're continuing, not restarting...

fact1.title: No Judgment Here
fact1.script: Life happens. Illness, travel, crisis, exhaustion—there are a thousand reasons to miss a day. None of them mean you've failed. The only failure is not returning.

fact2.title: Pick Up Anywhere
fact2.script: You don't need to catch up on missed lessons. You can, if you want. But you can also just continue from today. Either approach works. What matters is forward motion.

fact3.title: Prevent Future Gaps
fact3.script: What would help you stay consistent? Smaller daily commitment? Different time? Accountability partner? Identify one adjustment that might help, and try it.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The streak that matters isn't days in a row—it's lifetime commitment. You're still learning. You're still growing. That's what counts.

outro.script: Ready to continue your journey? Your next lesson awaits. The gap is behind you. The path is ahead. Let's keep going.

growTrack.title: Re-engagement Plan - Make Returning Easier
growTrack.activity: What caused the gap? What would make returning easier next time? Write down one adjustment to your routine. Set a reminder for tomorrow's lesson. You're back—let's stay back.
